figures.caption: Figure 1. Master summary of numerical results. Row 1: Loss landscape contours for the symmetric toy model (d = 1, m = 2, v = [1, 1]) at four values of λ; the diagonal w1 = w2 is marked in cyan. Row 2, left: Hessian eigenvalues along the diagonal branch showing S2-induced zero transverse eigenvalue at λ = 0. Row 2, right: Reduced potential along the anti-diagonal, showing monotonically deepening double well. Row 3, left: Full Hessian spectrum for the higher-dimensional model (d = 5, m = 10), with genuine eigenvalue crossing at λ∗ ≈ 0.72. Row 3, right: Zoomed eigenvalue tracking near λ∗ confirming simple kernel and nonzero crossing speed. Row 4: Reduced potential slices, polynomial fit, and 2D contours in the center manifold before and after bifurcation.

Figure 4. Width-scaling analysis. Top left: Spectral softening curves for m = 3 to m = 100; dots mark the zero-crossing λ∗. Top center: Bifurcation point λ∗ vs. width m, with first-order theoretical prediction and fit λ∗ ≈ 0.97 − 2.03/m. Top right: Log-log scaling of λ1(0) (constant = α) and |λ′ 1(0)| ∼ m−1.2. Bottom left: λ∗ vs. 1/m showing the linear relationship predicted by Eq. (23). Bottom center: Simple-kernel ratio |λ1/λ2| at λ∗. Bottom right: Theory vs. numerical λ∗.

Figure 5. Verification of explicit constants. Top row: Theory-vs-numerical comparison for W ∗(0) (Sylvester solution), eigenvalue trajectory with 1st/2nd-order predictions, and decomposition of gaa and gaaa into Gauss–Newton and residual contributions. Middle row: Width-scaling constant K from fitting λ′ 1(0) = K/m; constancy of λ′ 1(0) ·m; λ∗ theory vs. numerical; and λ1(0) = α verification. Bottom row: Theory-vs-numerical λ′ 1(0), reduced potential fit, overcritical λ1(1) check, and summary of all explicit constants.
Table 1. Summary of numerical results at the bifurcation point λ∗.

Figure 2. Transversality and solution-quality verification for the d = 5, m = 10 model. Left: The reduced coefficient c2(µ) is linear in µ = λ−λ∗ with slope ≈ 0.044, confirming nonzero transversality. Center: Loss along the continued branch; the bifurcation at λ∗ ≈ 0.72 is a spectral event, not a loss discontinuity. Right: Gradient norm along the branch, confirming that continuation tracks a genuine critical point.

Figure 3. Phase diagram for the bifurcation point. Left: Bifurcation parameter λ∗ as a function of the symmetry-breaking parameter α in the toy model v = [1, α]; circles denote interior crossings, crosses denote boundary degeneracies. Center: Spectral softening curves for selected α values. Right: Loss and minimum eigenvalue for the d = 5, m = 10 model.
